newsitem.title: USA: Chicago sewer to take less water from Lake Michigan.
newsitem.headline: Chicago sewer to take less water from Lake Michigan.

text.p: Eight states surrounding the Great Lakes settled a 90-year-old dispute over the use of Lake Michigan waters in Chicago's sewer system, the U.S. Justice Department said Wednesday.
The agreement called for Chicago to syphon off less water over the next 20 years, said Andy Walch, a Justice Department attorney involved in the negotiations.

An accounting system set up in 1980 found that the city had been diverting more water than it was allowed under an earlier agreement. But part of the problem was in how rainfall and ground water flows were being measured.

The settlement reached last week allows the state of Illinois to test over the next three years a new system for measuring how much water is being diverted from Lake Michigan and into the Mississippi River. The other Great Lakes states will also monitor efforts by Illinois to reduce water use.
The agreement helped the states avoid "a very lengthy, cumbersome" Supreme Court hearing process that would have cost millions of dollars, Justice Department attorney Peter Steenland said.
